# Agent discovery: Cloudflare and registrar handoff

Publish DNS discovery for `docs.eden.zone`. Josh can perform these steps if he has
the required access; otherwise, Cris or the domain owner can apply them. Merging
this document does not change DNS, enable DNSSEC, or deploy an authentication service.

## Which findings apply

| Scanner finding                           | Action for this documentation service                                        |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| DNS-AID entrypoint missing                | Publish the SVCB index record below and validate DNSSEC.                     |
| OAuth/OIDC discovery missing              | Not applicable: the docs do not operate an authorization server.             |
| OAuth protected resource metadata missing | Not applicable: the docs REST API and MCP endpoint are public and read-only. |
| `auth.md` missing                         | Not applicable: the docs do not register agents or issue credentials.        |

These decisions match the [public API guide](../docs/pages/use-the-docs-with-ai.mdx)
and routing in `worker/index.js`. Blockchain RPC providers have separate access
rules; this handoff applies only to the documentation service.

## 1. Confirm access and save the current state

- Open the `eden.zone` zone in the Cloudflare dashboard. Confirm you can edit its
  DNS records and DNSSEC settings. Access to the Pages project alone is insufficient.
- Confirm who can update DNSSEC at the domain registrar. If Josh lacks either
  permission, hand the corresponding step to Cris or the domain owner.
- Export the zone and record the existing DNSSEC/registrar DS state before editing.
  Check whether `_index._agents.docs.eden.zone` already exists; reconcile an existing
  record instead of adding a duplicate. Preserve unrelated records and the existing
  `docs.eden.zone` Pages routing and proxy settings.

## 2. Publish the DNS-AID index

In **eden.zone → DNS → Records**, add this record:

| Cloudflare field               | Value                 |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------- |
| Type                           | `SVCB`                |
| Name (relative to `eden.zone`) | `_index._agents.docs` |
| Priority                       | `1`                   |
| Target                         | `docs.eden.zone`      |
| Value / parameters             | `alpn="h2" port=443`  |
| TTL                            | `3600` (one hour)     |
| Proxy status                   | DNS only              |

Equivalent zone-file record:

```dns
_index._agents.docs.eden.zone. 3600 IN SVCB 1 docs.eden.zone. alpn="h2" port=443
```

This uses ServiceMode from [RFC 9460](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9460)
and the organizational index entrypoint in
[DNS-AID draft 02, section 3.2](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-mozleywilliams-dnsop-dnsaid-02.html#section-3.2).
DNS-AID is experimental; recheck the draft before changing the record format.
The index is scoped to `docs.eden.zone`, the scanned hostname, not all of `eden.zone`.
Do not advertise an `_a2a` endpoint: this service exposes MCP, not A2A.

The existing index is `https://docs.eden.zone/.well-known/ai-catalog.json`.
Its MCP entry links to `/api/mcp/server-card`, which identifies `/api/mcp`.
The catalog path is an application convention that clients must know: standard
SVCB `alpn` and `port` parameters do not encode it. This record supplies transport
discovery, not a universal catalog-path discovery mechanism. No experimental
custom SvcParamKey assignments are required for this configuration.

Confirm HTTP/2 support before publishing:

```bash
curl --fail --silent --show-error --http2 --output /dev/null \
  --write-out 'HTTP %{http_code}; version %{http_version}\n' \
  https://docs.eden.zone/.well-known/ai-catalog.json
```

Require HTTP `200` and version `2`. Cloudflare documents
[SVCB record support](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/).

## 3. Establish DNSSEC validation

Follow [Cloudflare's DNSSEC setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dnssec/):

1. Inspect **eden.zone → DNS → Settings → DNSSEC**. If signing is already enabled,
   preserve it; otherwise enable it.
2. At the registrar, publish the exact DS values generated by Cloudflare, unless
   the registrar handles this automatically. Do not invent DS values or add the
   apex DS as an ordinary record inside `eden.zone`.
3. Wait for the parent DS publication and DNS caches to update. Zone signing
   alone does not establish the public chain of trust.

DNSSEC affects the whole zone. Coordinate this step with its owner and preserve
any existing valid chain. Cloudflare Registrar can manage the parent update;
see its [DNSSEC instructions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/registrar/get-started/enable-dnssec/).

## 4. Verify and record completion

Run these queries against both validating resolvers. `TYPE64` is the numeric form
of SVCB and also works with older versions of `dig`:

```bash
dig @1.1.1.1 _index._agents.docs.eden.zone TYPE64 +dnssec
dig @8.8.8.8 _index._agents.docs.eden.zone TYPE64 +dnssec
dig @1.1.1.1 eden.zone DS +dnssec
dig @8.8.8.8 eden.zone DS +dnssec
curl -fsS https://docs.eden.zone/.well-known/ai-catalog.json
curl -fsS https://docs.eden.zone/api/mcp/server-card
```

Require `NOERROR`, the intended SVCB answer (priority, target, ALPN and port), the
provider-generated DS answer, and `ad` in both resolvers' response flags.
An empty answer, `SERVFAIL`, or a signature without `ad` is not completion.
Allow negative caches to expire if the name was queried before publication.

Confirm that anonymous MCP initialization still succeeds:

```bash
curl -fsS https://docs.eden.zone/api/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"discovery-check","version":"1.0"}}}'
```

Require a JSON-RPC `result` with `serverInfo.name` equal to `eden-docs`.
Rerun the [agent-readiness scanner](https://isitagentready.com/) for
`https://docs.eden.zone` using the same check selection as the original scan.
Record the timestamp, DNS responses, and DNS-AID result in the PR. If the scanner
still rejects the record, inspect its diagnostic before changing the published
service description. The three authentication findings remain not applicable.

### Rollback

Remove only the newly added SVCB record, or restore its saved previous value.
Leave Pages routing and valid DNSSEC intact. If DNSSEC itself must be rolled back,
remove the parent DS through the registrar and wait for its cached copies to
expire before disabling zone signing; disabling signing first can break resolution.

## If protected APIs are introduced later

Before adding authentication discovery, identify the actual resource owner,
issuer, supported scopes/grants, and registration flow. Then publish metadata
that matches the deployed service:

- Use [OIDC discovery](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-discovery-1_0.html)
  or [OAuth authorization server metadata](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8414)
  at the issuer, with its real supported endpoints and capabilities.
- Use [OAuth protected resource metadata](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9728)
  at the protected resource, identifying the issuers it actually trusts.
- Publish [auth.md](https://github.com/workos/auth.md) and applicable `agent_auth`
  metadata only for an implemented agent registration/provisioning flow.

Do not publish placeholder issuers, token endpoints, registration URLs, or scopes
to satisfy a scanner. Cloudflare dashboard access for maintainers does not make
the public documentation API an OAuth-protected resource.
